name: Kundt Waves
description: Exact gravitational waves on plane fronts whose rays turn from one front to the next. In flat space the fronts are half planes rolling round a cylinder that expands at the speed of light, and the cylinder is a singularity that no curvature scalar shows.
convention: The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Does a plane wave have to keep to one direction? The textbook ones do: on the pp-waves that Heinrich Brinkmann found in 1925 every ray is parallel to every other [brinkmann1925, ehlerskundt1962]. Wolfgang Kundt asked for more in 1961, and surveyed every radiation field whose rays neither spread apart nor twist around one another, the fields he called "plane-fronted" [kundt1961]. Those of his fields that are pure gravitational waves in empty space, the fields of type N, come in two families [bicak1999, griffiths2004]. One is the pp-waves [bicak1999]. The other, whose rays are parallel on any one front and point another way on the next, now carries Kundt's name [griffiths2004, podolskybelan2004].¶The picture came in 1998 from Jerry Griffiths and Jiří Podolský, and it holds wherever the wave is weak enough that the space it crosses is as good as flat [griffithspodolsky1998]. Imagine a cylinder whose radius grows at the speed of light, $X^2 + Z^2 = c^2T^2$, and lean a half plane against it so that the two touch along one line [griffithspodolsky1998, griffiths2004]. That half plane is a wave front, and it moves off at right angles to itself as the cylinder swells [griffiths2004]. The next front leans a little further round, and so on through a full turn, each one labelled by $u = \tan(\alpha/2)$ for its angle $\alpha$ [griffiths2004, podolskybelan2004]. An observer standing outside feels the wave's direction swing round until the cylinder itself arrives [griffiths2004].¶Kundt's waves are simplest in coordinates that ride on the fronts. There the metric is $$ds^2 = dx^2 + dy^2 - 4x^2\,du\,dv + 4\left(x^2v^2 + xG\right)du^2,$$ where $x = \sqrt{X^2 + Z^2 - c^2T^2}$ vanishes on the cylinder, $y$ runs along its axis, and $v$ runs along the rays [podolskybelan2004]. The profile $G(u, x, y)$ is free, and Einstein's equations in empty space ask only that it be harmonic on each front, $\partial_x^2 G + \partial_y^2 G = 0$ [podolskybelan2004]. Set $G = 0$ and the wave is gone, leaving flat space in unfamiliar coordinates [podolskybelan2004]. The fronts end at $x = 0$, and none of them reaches inside the cylinder [griffiths2004].¶Is anything wrong at the cylinder? Every scalar you can build from the curvature says no: for a wave of type N with rays like these all of them vanish, to every order of derivative, a theorem of Jiří Bičák and Vojtěch Pravda [bicakpravda1998, podolskybelan2004]. For the kindred fields of pure radiation, Griffiths and Podolský had proposed filling the inside with flat space, a void that the outgoing radiation leaves behind [griffithspodolsky1998]. Six years on, Podolský and Miroslav Beláň put the cylinder to the test by letting particles and light fall toward $x = 0$ [podolskybelan2004]. They arrive in a finite time by their own clocks, and the tidal forces on them grow without bound along the way [podolskybelan2004]. The cylinder is a curvature singularity that no scalar shows, and flat space cannot be joined smoothly to its inside [ellisschmidt1977, podolskybelan2004].¶When space itself is curved, what becomes of the two families? A cosmological constant came to Kundt's waves in 1981 at the hands of Alberto García Díaz and Jerzy Plebański, and four years later István Ozsváth, Ivor Robinson, and Krzysztof Rózga widened the family and sorted it by the sign of one invariant [garciadiaz1981, ozsvath1985, bicak1999]. By Bičák and Podolský's count of 1999 it has six kinds, among them the pp-waves, Kundt's waves, and the waves Stephen Siklos found crossing anti-de Sitter space [bicak1999, siklos1985]. In de Sitter space the fronts are hemispheres, the cylinder closes up into a torus, and the pp-waves and Kundt's waves are one family written in two sets of coordinates [griffiths2004]. In anti-de Sitter space the families are three, with Siklos's on the boundary between the other two [griffiths2004].¶Hunting in 2002 for every spacetime whose curvature scalars all vanish, Pravda, Alena Pravdová, Alan Coley, and Robert Milson found them all inside Kundt's class [pravda2002]. Coley showed the same year that such spacetimes solve string theory exactly, to all orders of perturbation [coley2002]. The class holds more than waves, since the universes of Nariai and of Bertotti and Robinson belong to it too [podolskybelan2004]. Podolský and Beláň left the far side of their wave open: $x \to \infty$ lies infinitely far away, some components of the curvature grow there along some paths and fade along others, and they called for a closer analysis of that infinity [podolskybelan2004].

related.text: The waves whose rays all stay parallel. In the coordinates of Ozsváth, Robinson, and Rózga, $\Lambda = 0$ and $\beta = 0$ leave a pp-wave in Brinkmann's form [ozsvath1985, bicak1999].
The waves that cross anti-de Sitter space with $\kappa = 0$. Set $\Lambda = -3/L^2$, $\alpha = 1$, and $\beta = 1/L$, and the metric is a Siklos wave on the disc [bicak1999, griffiths2004].
The wave switched off. With $G = 0$ the metric is flat space outside the cylinder $X^2 + Z^2 = c^2T^2$ [podolskybelan2004].
The space the waves with $\Lambda > 0$ cross. At $h = 0$ the metric is de Sitter space, and the fronts are hemispheres touching a torus that expands at the speed of light [bicak1999, griffiths2004].
The space the waves with $\Lambda < 0$ cross. At $h = 0$ the metric is anti-de Sitter space, and the fronts are hyperbolic planes [bicak1999, griffiths2004].
The waves whose rays spread apart. A wave of type N without twist is either one of Kundt's, whose rays do not expand, or one of Robinson and Trautman's [bicak1999].
A universe with rays that neither expand nor twist, which puts it in Kundt's class beside his waves [podolskybelan2004].
Another member of Kundt's class that is no wave, a universe filled with a uniform electromagnetic field [podolskybelan2004].

coordinates.name: Kundt
domains: x = 0 \;\text{(the envelope of the wave fronts)}

parameters.description: Wave profile, a length, a function of $u$ and of the two coordinates along the wave front. The spacetime is a vacuum exactly where it is harmonic on the front, $\partial_x^2 G + \partial_y^2 G = 0$; $G = 0$ is flat space, and so is any $G$ linear in $x$ and $y$

coordinates.convention: We use Kundt's canonical coordinates $(u, w, x, y)$: $u$ is a pure number labelling the wave fronts, $w$ an affine parameter along the rays carrying an area, and $x$ and $y$ lengths on the front. We leave the profile $G$ free, so no component assumes a field equation. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Podolský-Beláň
domains: x = 0 \;\text{(the envelope of the wave fronts)}

parameters.description: Wave profile, a length, a function of $u$ and of the two coordinates along the wave front. The spacetime is a vacuum exactly where it is harmonic on the front, $\partial_x^2 G + \partial_y^2 G = 0$; $G = 0$ is flat space, and so is any $G$ linear in $x$ and $y$

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(u, v, x, y)$ of Podolský and Beláň, with $u$ and $v$ pure numbers and $x$ and $y$ lengths; $w = 2x^2v$ is the affine parameter of Kundt's canonical form. We leave the profile $G$ free, so no component assumes a field equation. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Simplest Wave
domains: x = 0 \;\text{(the envelope of the wave fronts)}

parameters.description: A length setting the strength of the wave, $G = (x^2 - y^2)/\ell$. It has no invariant meaning: the rescaling $u \to \lambda u$, $v \to v/\lambda$ turns $\ell$ into $\lambda^2\ell$

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(u, v, x, y)$ of Podolský and Beláň, with $u$ and $v$ pure numbers and $x$ and $y$ lengths, and the profile $G = (x^2 - y^2)/\ell$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Kerr-Schild
domains: X^2 + Z^2 > c^2T^2 \;\text{(outside the envelope of the wave fronts)}
cT + Z = 0,\; X < 0 \;\text{(the wave front } u \to \pm\infty\text{)}

parameters.description: A length setting the strength of the wave, $G = (x^2 - Y^2)/\ell$
Distance along a wave front from the line where it touches the envelope, the cylinder $X^2 + Z^2 = c^2T^2$; it is the $x$ of Podolský and Beláň's coordinates
Label of the wave front through the event, $u = \tan(\alpha/2)$ for the front $cT = X\sin\alpha + Z\cos\alpha$
The coordinate $v$ of Podolský and Beláň, which runs along the rays

coordinates.convention: We use the inertial coordinates $(T, X, Y, Z)$ of the flat space the wave crosses, with $T$ carrying dimensions of time; the wave is $G = (x^2 - Y^2)/\ell$, and $x$, $u$, and $v$ are Podolský and Beláň's coordinates as functions of these. We take components in the chart $x^0 = cT$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{T}$ means $d(cT)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -c^2dT^2 + dX^2 + dY^2 + dZ^2 + \dfrac{x^2 - Y^2}{\ell x}\left(\left(1 + u^2\right)c\,dT - 2u\,dX - \left(1 - u^2\right)dZ\right)^2
geodesics: \ddot{T} + \dfrac{\left(u^2 + 1\right)^2\left(u^2\,v\,x^2 + u^2\,v\,Y^2 - u\,x^2 + 3u\,Y^2 + v\,x^2 + v\,Y^2\right)}{2x^2\,\ell}\dot{T}^2 - \dfrac{\left(u^2 + 1\right)\left(2u^3\,v\,x^2 + 2u^3\,v\,Y^2 - 3u^2\,x^2 + 5u^2\,Y^2 + 2u\,v\,x^2 + 2u\,v\,Y^2 + x^2 + Y^2\right)}{x^2\,\ell}\dot{T}\dot{X} + \dfrac{2Y\left(u^2 + 1\right)^2}{x\,\ell}\dot{T}\dot{Y} + \dfrac{\left(u^2 + 1\right)\left(u^4\,v\,x^2 + u^4\,v\,Y^2 - u^3\,x^2 + 3u^3\,Y^2 + 3u\,x^2 - u\,Y^2 - v\,x^2 - v\,Y^2\right)}{x^2\,\ell}\dot{T}\dot{Z} + \dfrac{2u\left(u^3\,v\,x^2 + u^3\,v\,Y^2 - 2u^2\,x^2 + 2u^2\,Y^2 + u\,v\,x^2 + u\,v\,Y^2 + x^2 + Y^2\right)}{x^2\,\ell}\dot{X}^2 - \dfrac{4u\,Y\left(u^2 + 1\right)}{x\,\ell}\dot{X}\dot{Y} - \dfrac{2u^5\,v\,x^2 + 2u^5\,v\,Y^2 - 3u^4\,x^2 + 5u^4\,Y^2 + 8u^2\,x^2 - 2u\,v\,x^2 - 2u\,v\,Y^2 - x^2 - Y^2}{x^2\,\ell}\dot{X}\dot{Z} + \dfrac{2Y\left(u^2 + 1\right)\left(u^2 - 1\right)}{x\,\ell}\dot{Y}\dot{Z} + \dfrac{\left(u^2 - 1\right)\left(u^4\,v\,x^2 + u^4\,v\,Y^2 - u^3\,x^2 + 3u^3\,Y^2 + 5u\,x^2 + u\,Y^2 - v\,x^2 - v\,Y^2\right)}{2x^2\,\ell}\dot{Z}^2 = 0

\ddot{Z} - \dfrac{\left(u^2 + 1\right)\left(u^4\,v\,x^2 + u^4\,v\,Y^2 - u^3\,x^2 + 3u^3\,Y^2 - 5u\,x^2 - u\,Y^2 - v\,x^2 - v\,Y^2\right)}{2x^2\,\ell}\dot{T}^2 + \dfrac{2u^5\,v\,x^2 + 2u^5\,v\,Y^2 - 3u^4\,x^2 + 5u^4\,Y^2 - 8u^2\,x^2 - 2u\,v\,x^2 - 2u\,v\,Y^2 - x^2 - Y^2}{x^2\,\ell}\dot{T}\dot{X} - \dfrac{2Y\left(u^2 + 1\right)\left(u^2 - 1\right)}{x\,\ell}\dot{T}\dot{Y} - \dfrac{\left(u^2 - 1\right)\left(u^4\,v\,x^2 + u^4\,v\,Y^2 - u^3\,x^2 + 3u^3\,Y^2 - 3u\,x^2 + u\,Y^2 - v\,x^2 - v\,Y^2\right)}{x^2\,\ell}\dot{T}\dot{Z} - \dfrac{2u\left(u^3\,v\,x^2 + u^3\,v\,Y^2 - 2u^2\,x^2 + 2u^2\,Y^2 - u\,v\,x^2 - u\,v\,Y^2 - x^2 - Y^2\right)}{x^2\,\ell}\dot{X}^2 + \dfrac{4u\,Y\left(u^2 - 1\right)}{x\,\ell}\dot{X}\dot{Y} + \dfrac{\left(u^2 - 1\right)\left(2u^3\,v\,x^2 + 2u^3\,v\,Y^2 - 3u^2\,x^2 + 5u^2\,Y^2 - 2u\,v\,x^2 - 2u\,v\,Y^2 - x^2 - Y^2\right)}{x^2\,\ell}\dot{X}\dot{Z} - \dfrac{2Y\left(u^2 - 1\right)^2}{x\,\ell}\dot{Y}\dot{Z} - \dfrac{\left(u^2 - 1\right)^2\left(u^2\,v\,x^2 + u^2\,v\,Y^2 - u\,x^2 + 3u\,Y^2 - v\,x^2 - v\,Y^2\right)}{2x^2\,\ell}\dot{Z}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Ozsváth-Robinson-Rózga
domains: p > 0 \;\text{(where } \Lambda < 0 \text{ the disc whose rim is the conformal boundary)}
q = 0 \;\text{(the envelope of the wave fronts)}

parameters.description: Cosmological constant, an inverse area of either sign or zero
A pure number. With $\beta = 0$ and $\Lambda = 0$ the metric is a pp-wave in Brinkmann's form
An inverse length. With $\alpha = 0$ and $\Lambda = 0$ the metric is a Kundt wave, and with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$, $\alpha = 1$, and $\beta = 1/L$ a Siklos wave

Wave profile of this chart, a dimensionless function of $u$, $\xi$, and $\eta$. The metric solves Einstein's equations with the cosmological constant $\Lambda$ and no matter exactly where $p^2(\partial_\xi^2 h + \partial_\eta^2 h) + 2\Lambda h/3 = 0$
Conformal factor of the wave front, a surface of constant curvature $\Lambda/3$
The second function of Ozsváth, Robinson, and Rózga; the envelope of the wave fronts is $q = 0$

The invariant of Ozsváth, Robinson, and Rózga, whose sign no change of coordinates alters: with $\Lambda = 0$ it vanishes for the pp-waves and is positive for Kundt's waves, and with $\Lambda < 0$ it vanishes for Siklos's

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates of Ozsváth, Robinson, and Rózga, all lengths, with $\alpha$ and $\beta$ constants and $\beta$ real. We leave the profile $h$ free, so no component assumes a field equation. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
